title: wattson power model
description: The ENERGY half of P = sum(energy_per_event * event_count). Supplied by the power team, NOT by QEMU. QEMU never emits a milliwatt: it emits the activity vector (wattson/activity-vector/v1) and this document says what each unit of that activity costs. Coefficients come either from measured silicon rails or, before tapeout, from gate-level estimation - which one is a required field, because a DERIVED coefficient and a MEASURED one may not be compared as if they were the same kind of number.

part.description: silicon this model describes, e.g. 'i.MX 95'. A model is not portable across parts: the coefficients embed process, library and microarchitecture.

provenance.description: MEASURED: fitted to real rails on real silicon. GATE_ESTIMATE: from synthesis/netlist power estimation, pre-tapeout. MIXED: some blocks each way, in which case every block MUST carry its own provenance.

conditions.description: The conditions the coefficients were obtained under. A coefficient is only valid here. Frequency in particular does NOT transfer - refitting an i.MX 95 core model at 900 MHz produced different coefficients with different signs, not a scaled version of the 1800 MHz set.

voltage_domain.description: rail these coefficients are expressed on, e.g. 'vdd_arm'

temperature_c.description: die temperature; leakage is temperature-dependent and QEMU models none of it

blocks.description: block name -> its power terms. Block names MUST match the names used in the activity vector, since the two documents are joined on them.

provenance.description: required when the model-level provenance is MIXED

static_mw.description: always-on cost when the block is powered but idle. Counted ONCE per block - summing a whole-system idle figure per block is the classic way to over-design a thermal solution by 3x.

terms.description: linear terms. P_block = static_mw + sum(coeff * activity[activity_key]).

activity_key.description: dotted path into the activity vector, e.g. 'peripherals.enetc.throughput_gbps'. The join is on this exact key: a coefficient fitted against DRAM READ traffic must name a read key, so that feeding it total read+write traffic fails loudly instead of silently over-predicting.

unit.description: unit of the activity quantity, e.g. 'Gbps', 'GB/s', 'Mops/s', 'cores', 'fraction'. Checked against the activity vector's declared unit; a mismatch is an error, not a warning.

valid_range.description: [min, max] of the activity quantity over which the coefficient was obtained. Predicting outside it is extrapolation and must be reported as such - an i.MX 95 core model fitted to 14 GB/s held to 1.3% on a read stream at 5.5 GB/s but over-predicted 12-13% on a write-heavy stream, because one bandwidth term charges reads and writes alike.
